items.stem: Internal audit’s role in enterprise risk management is best described as:

options.text: Providing independent assurance over the effectiveness of risk management
options.rationale: Correct: internal audit gives independent assurance on risk management effectiveness.

options.text: Owning and accepting all enterprise risks
options.rationale: Management owns risk; audit provides assurance, not ownership.

options.text: Setting the organization’s risk appetite alone
options.rationale: Risk appetite is set by the board/management, not audit alone.
Audit assures risk management; it does not replace it.

items.explanation: Correct: internal audit gives independent assurance on risk management effectiveness.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: To preserve objectivity, internal auditors providing assurance over a process should generally avoid:

options.text: Having designed or operated the control they are now auditing
options.rationale: Correct: auditing one’s own work impairs objectivity.
Reviewing documentation is a normal audit activity.
Interviews are a standard, acceptable audit technique.

options.text: Reporting findings to the audit committee
options.rationale: Reporting to the audit committee supports independence.

items.explanation: Correct: auditing one’s own work impairs objectivity.

items.stem: Select TWO inputs that support risk-based audit planning.

options.text: The organization’s risk assessment and risk register
options.rationale: Correct: the risk register helps prioritize audit effort by risk.

options.text: Input from management and the board on key concerns
options.rationale: Correct: stakeholder input informs where assurance is most needed.

options.text: Auditing areas strictly in alphabetical order
Avoiding any area that is considered high risk
options.rationale: High-risk areas should be prioritized, not avoided.

items.explanation: Correct: the risk register helps prioritize audit effort by risk.
